messages.subject: Formulating error in covariates logistic regression model in Stan
parts:
Hi there,

I'm trying to recode a former openbugs project in stan, so far unsuccessfuly. The background is the following: I have a binary response (Y), and a O predictors associated with my response measured with error for N observations. In my particular data setting, I know exactly the values that the covariate vector may take. The BUGS model for this data is:

model {
        for (i in 1:N) {
                Y[i]~dbern (p[i])
                p[i] <- 1/(1+exp(-z[i]))
                z[i] <- betas[1]+betas[2]*env1[i]+betas[3]*env2[i]+betas[4]*env1sq[i]
                env1[i] <- env1Table[i,k[i]]
                env2[i] <- env2Table[i,k[i]]
                env1sq[i] <- env1sqTable[i,k[i]]
                k[i]~dcat(pcatTable[i,])
        }
        betas[1] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
        betas[2] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
        betas[3] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
        betas[4] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
}

My translation of this model to Stan is:

logistic.cauchy.error<-'data {
  int<lower=0> N; // number of sites
  int<lower=0> M; // number of possible covariate vector values per site
  int<lower=0> O; // number of regression coefficients
  matrix[N,M] env1Table; // predictor env1matrix. Rows are observations.
  matrix[N,M] env2Table; // predictor env2matrix. Rows are observations.
  matrix[N,M] env1sqTable; // predictor env1sq matrix. Rows are observations.
  matrix[N,M] pcatTable; // predictor probabilities matrix. Rows are observations.
  int<lower=0,upper=1> Y[N];// response vector
}
parameters {
  real beta[O];
  real k[N];
}
model {
  for (j in 1:O)
    beta[j] ~ normal(0,100);
  for (n in 1:N)
    k[n] ~ categorical(pcatTable[n,1:M]);
    env1[n] <- env1Table[n,k[n]];
    env2[n] <- env2Table[n,k[n]];
    env1sq[n] <- env1sqTable[n,k[n]];
    Y[n] ~ bernoulli(inv_logit(beta[1]+beta[2]*env1[i]+beta[3]*env2[i]+beta[4]*env1sq[i]));
}'

However, after trying to fit this model I get the error:

EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=21, column=37

    k[n] ~ categorical(pcatTable[n,1:M]);
                                    ^-- here


DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Parser expecting: "]"

It seems I'm not properly indexing the pcatTable matrix, or in any case that pcatTable[n,1:M] is not read as a vector. Any clues on how to fix this?

Thanks!

Jorge Velásquez

parts:
Stan is not R, especially when it comes to matrix slicing and dicing.  
Please see the “row” and “col” functions in the manual.

Also, watch out on the beta priors — Stan uses N(mu, sigma) so for
an equivalent model you’ll want normal(0, 10).  Additionally, the
priors can be vectorized — just replace the loop with
beta ~ normal(0, 10).  Lastly, bernoulli_logit() will perform much
better than bernoulli(inv_logit()).

parts:
DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name="categorical_log"
    arg 0 type=real
    arg 1 type=vector
available function signatures for categorical_log:
0.  categorical_log(int, vector) : real
1.  categorical_log(int[1], vector) : real
unknown distribution=categorical
Parser expecting: <eps>

Categorical has two inputs, an integer and a vector of probabilities, and one output, a real-valued log probability density.
Your model defines k as a vector of reals, not integers, hence you're trying to insert a real into the integer argument which is causing the conflict.

The bigger problem is that you can't just make k an array of integers as Stan does not do discrete sampling.  You would only be able
to use the categorical distribution if your _data_ were distributed as a categorical, not any of your model parameters.
